Think on the Graph: every output of the run MY10

0. Input

Program:

int[] a = {5, 10, 15};
for (int i = 0; i <= a.length; i++) {
    System.out.println(a[i]);
}

Question: What does this program print, and why?

Student's answer: It prints 0, then 5, 10 and 15. Arrays start at a[1], so a[0] is before the first element and just gives 0. Then a[1], a[2] and a[3] are 5, 10 and 15. Settings: width 3, depth 3, prune llm, backend claude-cli, model claude-opus-5-5

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:indexing->ArrayAccessWithParentheses | wrong rule: a(i) accesses element i of an array. | right rule: Array elements are accessed with square brackets, a[i]. | | mis:indexing->ArrayElementNotVariable | wrong rule: An array element a[i] is not a variable, so it cannot be read into directly or used inside another index, as in a[a[i]]. | right rule: Each element a[i] is a variable of the element type and can be used anywhere a variable of that type can, including as an index. | | mis:indexing->ArrayIndexStartsAtOne | wrong rule: The first element of a is a[1]. | right rule: Numbering begins with 0; the first element is a[0]. | | mis:indexing->ArrayRangeInclusive | wrong rule: new int[n] has slots 0 to n, inclusive. | right rule: The slots are 0 to n - 1. | | mis:indexing->ArrayUseScansAllCells | wrong rule: Using an array means every cell must be scanned. | right rule: Arrays allow random access: a[i] reaches one element directly, and a loop visits only the elements the task needs. | | mis:indexing->ElementBoundToOldIndex | wrong rule: After i changes, X[i] still refers to the element at the old value of i. | right rule: a[i] is evaluated with the current value of i each time it is used. | | mis:indexing->ElementNameIsWholeArray | wrong rule: X[i] names the whole array, not one element. | right rule: The array is a; a[i] is the single element at index i. | | mis:indexing->IndexIsValue | wrong rule: i and a[i] are the same thing, so the position is the stored value. | right rule: i is a position; a[i] is the value stored at that position. |

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:array_traversal->EarlyReturnInLoop | wrong rule: Leaves a traversal loop with return before every element has been processed. | right rule: A result that depends on all elements is known only after the loop ends. | | mis:array_traversal->ArrayUseScansAllCells | wrong rule: Using an array means every cell must be scanned. | right rule: Arrays allow random access: a[i] reaches one element directly, and a loop visits only the elements the task needs. | | mis:array_traversal->ElementBoundToOldIndex | wrong rule: After i changes, X[i] still refers to the element at the old value of i. | right rule: a[i] is evaluated with the current value of i each time it is used. | | mis:array_traversal->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:array_traversal->OffByOneBound | wrong rule: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable | right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n. | | mis:array_traversal->WholeArrayArithmetic | wrong rule: a = a + b adds the arrays element by element. | right rule: Java has no arithmetic on whole arrays; write a loop that adds a[i] + b[i] for each i. |
